summary: w211 research done; notes.md in the run directory, parts 1-7. All 26 accepted scenarios fail at their first Given (undefined steps, run). Probes (run) show: asker's requests land in the asker's own repo (r28/r44); --source with --thread accepted and sources dropped (r30); asker id from another context accepted (r32); outcome/reply accepted from the wrong side (r33/r34); a title with a newline sets status accepted after turn (r43); work show <request> refused (r25); no take-in command exists (r39-r43). Carrier for 'sent' and the asker-id allow list are not in spec or code. Conflicts for the plan: work-queue r7 lines-file scenario vs r30 ordering; supervision raise writes into the upstream's checkout vs r28; Retires cites @r44/@r45 where the feature tags @r1/@r3. Disclosed: I ran `tools map --json` once, against the brief. test_work_queue.py cannot be collected under the work_items plugin, so its r7 claim is read only.
questions: Carrier of 'sent' (r39-r43) and the upstream's asker-id allow list (decision 0071): no mechanism or list location in spec or code. Git transport of requests files, or a drop directory?

work-queue r7 scenario (lines file missing, --source, asker ctx-a, features/work-queue.feature:304) conflicts with r30 if the origin check runs before the file check. Keep the order (test stays) or change the scenario?
supervision raise (r135) writes requests into the upstream's checkout; under r28 read for every writer, features/supervision.feature:1445-1452 cannot pass. Does r28 bind supervision's raise?
Work-item Retires cites requests @r44 and @r45 for the deprecated titles, but features/requests.feature tags those titles @r1 and @r3; @r44 and @r45 are the live scenarios. Which tags are meant?
A request with an empty lines file is accepted with no lines (probe K). Refuse it, or accept it?
